Hey Logan,

Our execs want a short note that lays out how Phoenix should think about a Dedicated capacity purchase: H100 vs A100 vs L4 for our two main workloads — (1) long-context retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with 2M token active KV footprint, and (2) high-concurrency embedding/indexing pipelines.

Key asks:
- A simple recommendation on tiering across H100/A100/L4 given constrained budget (we have to cap committed spend for Q1).
- Node counts and expected headroom for 99th pct latency targets: 150ms for RAG generation, 30ms for embeddings.
- Failure/fallback behavior if a node runs out of memory for a long-context request.

I've attached a CSV with our workload profiles (phx-workload-profiles.csv). Can we get a short playbook and a call next week to walk the choices? Ops (ops@phoenix-ai.com) is on the thread for sizing.

Cheers,

Sara —

Thanks for the profile. Quick read looks like two dominant patterns: large KV cache + occasional very long prefixes for RAG, and steady high-rate short-context embedding jobs. High level guidance up-front:

- H100: prioritize for long-context RAG where model activations and KV cache per-session push beyond 80GB uncached; best for throughput on long sequences and lower prefilling cost.
- A100: sweet spot for mid-length generation and mixed workloads where memory density + cost balance matters.
- L4: optimized for low-latency, cost-sensitive embedding traffic and can act as a quantized fallback for shorter-generation variants.

I'll put together a compact decision table and a fallback runbook. See preliminary reference attached (redwood-gpu-reference-2026.pdf).

Two immediate clarifying items for the sizing calc before I send numbers:
1) What is your peak steady-state RAG QPS and peak burst multiplier (e.g., 3x for traffic bursts)?
2) Do you require single-tenant nodes for PHX sensitive routes or is multi-tenant Dedicated acceptable?

If you can share answers today I'll aim to circulate a 1-page playbook by Thu PST and propose a Wednesday call (30m).

—Logan

Sara / Logan —

Putting in a concise proposal for PHX based on the CSV and Logan's notes. TL;DR recommendation: tiered fleet with explicit roles. Attachment: phx-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf (short proposal + cost run).

Recommendation (baseline commit sizing):
- RAG (primary): 6 x H100 nodes (80GB), pinned to the RAG model family. Rationale: supports 2M-token KV windows via segmented KV caching; model prefills amortized over larger batch sizes. Expected steady QPS supported: ~25 QPS with 20% headroom at 99th pct < 180ms; burst tolerance to 50 QPS with autoscale policies.
- Mixed-generation: 10 x A100 nodes (40GB) for mid-length generation and as overflow for RAG short sessions. Expected for general NLG features and can be used for canary rollouts.
- Embeddings & low-latency inference: 12 x L4 nodes (quantized 8-bit preferred). L4 handles the embedding QPS target with 30ms p99 and acts as cheap fallback for short-form generation when economical.

Cost tradeoffs and notes:
- H100 per-node cost is ~3x L4 on our dedicated pricing; recommend keeping H100 to the minimal set that prevents KV eviction.
- For serialization-heavy RAG sessions we recommend a KV-prefetch layer (in-memory prefix cache) sized at ~200GB total across the H100 pool to reduce cold-cache prefills.
- If committed budget is limiting, consider 4 H100 + 12 A100 (use A100 for some long-context sessions with reduced context windows and model distillation).

Failure/fallback and ops playbook (short):
1) If an H100 node hits OOM on a request: route that session to an A100 with shortened context and emit a client-level partial-result header.
2) If A100 capacity exhausted, fall back to L4 quantized variant for embeddings and short responses with confidence scoring.
3) Implement prefix/KV hit-rate monitoring: alert when miss-rate > 12% sustained over 5m — trigger prewarmed nodes and raise autoscale multiplier.

I'll include expected cost ranges and a simple node-count sensitivity sheet in the attached PDF. Happy to run the numbers on your actual QPS if you confirm bursts and tenancy.

—Marissa

Sara / PHX ops —

Following up with an operational playbook for the failure modes you asked about. This is intentionally terse so your SREs can fold it into runbooks.

Operational sizing & failover checklist:
- Node mix baseline: H100 6 / A100 10 / L4 12 (see Marissa). Assume 10% steady-state spare capacity for safe autoscaler thresholds.
- KV cache strategy: shard KV store across H100 nodes using 128MB tiles with LRU eviction. Aim for a hot-set replication factor of 2 for high-p99 availability.
- Prefill vs. demand fill: prefill heavy sessions during low-cost windows (overnight) when possible; if prefill latency > 500ms, treat as cold and route to A100 with a reduced context window.
- Memory pressure handling: implement a graceful degradation handler that does the following in order: 1) drop oldest prefix tiles (smallest impact on semantics), 2) trigger model quantized fallback on L4 for non-critical paths, 3) return partial results with 'incomplete_context' header for client reconciliation.
- Autoscale policy suggestion: base on 60s rolling QPS and p95 latency. Trigger scale-out at 70% GPU util or when prefix cache miss-rate > 10% for 2m. Scale-in only after 10m sustained below 40% util.
- Canary/rollout guidance: route 5% of traffic to quantized variants on L4 to surface quality regressions early; monitor generation divergence metrics against a held prompt set.

Sizing quick-calcs (for your CSV, assumptions):
- H100: 6 nodes -> supports ~25 steady QPS RAG (2M token context) with 20% headroom. Each H100 node holds ~350GB of effective working set when we combine tiled KV in RAM & on-gpu swap techniques.
- A100: 10 nodes -> supports ~60 QPS mixed generation; useful as spillover and for mid-length sessions to avoid costly H100 cycles.
- L4: 12 nodes -> supports embeddings at target p99 < 30ms and up to 400 QPS embedding throughput when batched at 64.

Next steps:
1) PHX to confirm peak steady QPS and burst multiplier.
2) We can run a 48h pilot with reduced commit (4 H100 + 6 A100 + 8 L4) for empirical latency/kv-miss data.
3) If pilot meets p99 targets, move to the baseline commit with a 45-day ramp and included autoscaler thresholds.

If you want, we can sketch the exact scale schedule for a 48h pilot and include Grafana dashboards and alert thresholds in the pilot handoff.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call tomorrow to review the pilot plan.

—Logan
